title: Energy Conversion and Efficiency
seo_title: Energy Efficiency Worksheets: Conversions, Power, Ohm's Law and kWh (High School Physics)
standard_text: Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another form of energy.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on energy conversion and efficiency (NGSS HS-PS3-3): energy conversions, efficiency, power, Ohm's law, kilowatt-hours and design constraints. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Efficiency = useful output ÷ input; the rest becomes heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

Devices change energy from one form to another, but never perfectly.

  • Efficiency = useful output ÷ input × 100%. The rest is wasted, mostly as heat, but not destroyed.
  • Power P = E ÷ t (watts). Electric power P = VI; Ohm's law I = V ÷ R. Energy in kWh = kW × hours.
  • Good designs meet the criteria (goals) within the constraints (limits like cost).
Example

Input 500 J, useful 150 J. Efficiency?

150 ÷ 500 × 100

Answer: 30%

Example

1,500 W heater for 4 h. Energy?

1.5 kW × 4 h

Answer: 6 kWh

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a device can be more than 100% efficient.
  • Thinking wasted energy disappears.
  • Thinking kilowatt-hours measure power.
